data.name: Sajdah

in_arabic.name: سجدة
in_arabic.long_meaning: سجدة هي كلمة عربية تعني الركوع في الصلاة، وهي من أهم أركان الصلاة في الإسلام، وتمثل الخضوع والخッシュة لله تعالى، وتستخدم في القرآن الكريم في العديد من الآيات لوصف الركوع والخضوع لله

in_urdu.name: سجدہ
in_urdu.meaning: نماز میں سر کو زمین پر رکھنا
in_urdu.long_meaning: سجدہ عربي زبان کا لفظ ہے جس کا مطلب نماز میں سر کو زمین پر رکھنا ہے، یہ اسلام میں نماز کے اہم ارکان میں سے ایک ہے، اور یہ اللہ تعالی کے سامنے جھکنے اور عاجزی کا اظہار کرتا ہے

in_hindi.name: सजदा
in_hindi.meaning: नमाज में सर को जमीन पर रखना
in_hindi.long_meaning: सजदा अरबी भाषा का शब्द है जिसका अर्थ नमाज में सर को जमीन पर रखना है, यह इस्लाम में नमाज के महत्वपूर्ण अंगों में से एक है, और यह अल्लाह तआला के सामने झुकने और विनम्रता का प्रदर्शन करता है

in_english.name: Sajdah
in_english.long_meaning: Sajdah is an Arabic term meaning prostration in prayer, it is one of the crucial elements of prayer in Islam, representing humility and submission to Allah, and is used in the Quran to describe prostration and submission to God

data.cultural_impact: The Sajdah prayer position signifies utmost reverence and submission to Allah (God in Islam). It is an essential component of Islamic prayer, and Muslims around the world perform this position five times a day. The practice of Sajdah is not only a demonstration of faith but also a unifying experience that bonds Muslims together, transcending cultural and linguistic differences. It reflects the cultural richness and diversity of the Islamic community, as various practices and customs may surround the ritual, such as the use of prayer rugs or the recitation of specific supplications.
data.spiritual_significance: The Sajdah prayer position holds immense spiritual significance for Muslims, symbolizing dependence on and obedience to Allah. It is a act of surrender and humility, allowing one to connect deeply with their faith and source of guidance, becoming a moment of personal introspection and communion between the individual and the Divine. Through Sajdah, Muslims reaffirm their commitment to their spiritual practice and seek Allah's mercy and forgiveness, ultimately strengthening their bond with their faith.
